content: Acetohexamide is an oral hypoglycemic medication that has been linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular mortality. It is essential to discuss the potential risks, benefits, and alternative treatments with your doctor before using this medication. Acetohexamide is prescribed to manage type II diabetes (non-insulin-dependent diabetes), particularly in individuals whose condition cannot be controlled by diet alone. This medication works by stimulating the pancreas to produce insulin and improving the body's ability to use insulin effectively. However, it requires a functioning pancreas to be effective and is not suitable for treating type I diabetes (insulin-dependent diabetes). In some cases, acetohexamide may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Acetohexamide is available in tablet form and should be taken orally as directed by your doctor. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking acetohexamide even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. Before starting acetohexamide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are taking. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney, liver, thyroid, or heart disease, or if you have had a severe infection. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. Acetohexamide should not be taken during pregnancy. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking acetohexamide. Additionally, avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as this medication may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet, and consult your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while taking acetohexamide, as alcohol can lower blood sugar levels. If you forget to take a dose of acetohexamide, ask your doctor in advance what to do in such situations. As a general rule, take the missed dose as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next dose. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Be aware of the symptoms of low and high blood sugar and know how to respond if they occur. Hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) may occur while taking this medication. Your doctor will provide instructions on how to manage hypoglycemia, which may include checking your blood sugar levels, consuming a food or beverage containing sugar (e.g., hard candy or fruit juice), or seeking medical care. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, nervousness, irritability, sudden mood changes, headache, numbness or tingling around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, and clumsy or jerky movements. If left untreated, severe symptoms such as confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness may develop. Ensure that family, friends, and others around you are aware of these symptoms and know to seek immediate medical attention if they occur. Hyperglycemia (high blood sugar) symptoms include extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, weakness, and blurred vision. If untreated, hyperglycemia can lead to a life-threatening condition called diabetic ketoacidosis. Symptoms of ketoacidosis include dry mouth, upset stomach, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, and decreased consciousness. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Acetohexamide may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience a skin rash, itching, redness, exaggerated sunburn, yellowing of the skin or eyes, light-colored stools, dark urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, fever, or sore throat. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store acetohexamide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for monitoring. Your doctor will order tests to evaluate your response to acetohexamide. To monitor its effectiveness, measure your blood or urine sugar levels using special test strips, tablets, or a blood glucose meter. Your doctor may also ask you to test your urine for ketones. Follow your doctor’s instructions for testing and recording results. If your blood sugar is high or if sugar or ketones are present in your urine, contact your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
